Despite the power of calls for a singular global science, I discovered environmental knowledge only in the joints of cultural and political encounter. Despite imperial standards for civil society, I have wandered into coalitions built on awkwardly linked incompatibilities. The projects I have studied self-consciously reach across the world, drawing their substance, support, and legitimacy from global sources. They deploy the rhetoric of the universal even as they shape its meanings to their particular processes of proliferation, scale-making, generalization, cosmopolitanism, or collaboration. They require us to follow calls to the universal without assuming these calls will foster the same conditions everywhere. This means grounding one’s analysis of global connection not in abstract principles of power and knowledge but rather in concrete engagements.

尽管有资本主义的标准化和整合，我发现，要了解资源开采，就不可能不把分析拖入加里曼丹边疆的傲慢与绝望。尽管有对单一全球科学的强大呼吁，我只在文化与政治遭遇的接缝中发现环境知识。尽管有对公民社会的帝国标准，我游荡进建立在别扭连接的不相容性之上的联盟。我研究的项目自觉伸向世界，从全球来源获取其实质、支持和合法性。它们部署普遍物的修辞，同时把其意义塑造成适合自己特定的增殖、尺度制造、概括、世界主义或协作过程。它们要求我们追随对普遍物的召唤，而不假定这些召唤会在各地促成相同条件。这意味着把对全球联结的分析奠定在具体的介入关系中，而不是权力与知识的抽象原则中。

This is a research strategy that aims to encourage critical purchase without cutting off the springs of hope. Hope is most important when things are going badly in the world; in the face of almost certain destruction, hope is a Gramscian optimism of the will. Such “unrealistic” hope begins in considering the possibility that tiny cracks might yet break open the dam; contingent openings are sites of unexpected force—for better or worse.
这是一种研究策略，旨在鼓励批判效力，同时不切断希望的泉源。当世界境况糟糕时，希望最为重要；面对几乎确定的毁灭，希望是葛兰西式的意志乐观主义。这种“不切实际”的希望始于考虑这样的可能性：微小裂缝仍可能冲开大坝；偶然的开口是意外力量的场所——无论好坏。

Political initiatives that work to reclaim forests for forest-dwelling communities respond to the conditions of theft and violence in which forest resources have become objects of frontier desire. I’m not sure these initiatives will work, and I’m sure they won’t bring justice to everyone. They embroil participants in debates about authenticity and consensus. They mess with—or displace—earlier categories and cosmologies; they realign local priorities. They require what Levi and Dean (2003) call the “risk” of indigeneity, that is, the strategic transformation of local identity to enter a wider conversation. To be taken seriously by national and imperial interlocutors requires some such risk.

为森林居民社群夺回森林的政治倡议，回应了森林资源成为边疆欲望对象的盗窃与暴力条件。我不确定这些倡议会奏效，我也确定它们不会为每个人带来正义。它们使参与者卷入关于真实性与共识的辩论。它们搅乱——或取代——早先的范畴和宇宙论；它们重新排列地方优先事项。它们需要列维和迪恩（Levi and Dean，2003）所谓的原住民性的“风险”，即战略性地转变地方身份，以进入更广泛的对话。要被国家和帝国对话者认真对待，就需要某种这样的风险。

Initiatives such as community resource management have gained substance through their contact with transnational institutions, such as the Ford Foundation. They have brought bureaucrats and entrepreneurs into their schemes, variously advancing, diluting, and co-opting their cause. Political gains and compromises can only be assessed through constant attention to these kinds of collaborations and their effects. There are no guarantees. An appreciation of erasure and abrasion among different forms of practical knowledge, as these create emergent solidarities and gaps, can help keep us honest. For myself, I am inclined to be generous with projects as long as I see how they strain against the common-sense forms that hold us to destruction and injustice as business as usual.
像社群资源管理这样的倡议，通过接触福特基金会等跨国机构而获得实质。它们把官僚和企业家带入其方案，以各种方式推进、稀释和收编其事业。政治收益与妥协只能通过持续关注这类协作及其效果来评估。没有保证。理解不同实践知识形式之间的抹除与磨损——当它们创造新兴团结与空隙时——有助于让我们保持诚实。对我自己来说，只要我看到项目如何竭力反抗那些把我们束缚于毁灭和不义之“一切照常”的常识形式，我就倾向于宽待它们。

Utopian critiques are critical perspectives we cannot do without—even if they will not be realized. The struggle for community-managed forests in Indonesia is a good example of a mobilization that inspires utopian, and indeed romantic, hopes. Its most tangible product so far has been the formation of a fragile overlapping agenda among environmental activists, nature loving students, and rural community spokespeople. Occasionally, this alliance has kept the forest from being destroyed for a few years, here and there. This is not so bad: Public forests worldwide are threatened and at best tentatively preserved. Meanwhile, the alliance itself revives the promise of democracy. Critics quite correctly point to crippling class disparities between students and farmers; still, perhaps it is the best thing about the alliance that such differences have not discouraged the participants. All of us need a little of the romanticism and commitment of these urban middle-class young people. Through them, the utopianism of a mobilization for the environment as justice becomes a challenge rather than a reason to give up.

乌托邦批评是我们不能缺少的批判视角——即使它们不会被实现。印尼争取社群管理森林的斗争是一个很好的例子，说明一场动员如何激发乌托邦——甚至浪漫——的希望。它迄今最切实的产物，是在环保活动家、热爱自然的学生和乡村社群发言人之间形成一个脆弱的重叠议程。偶尔，这个联盟在这里或那里让森林免遭毁灭几年。这不算太糟：全世界的公共森林都受到威胁，最多只能暂时得到保护。与此同时，联盟本身复兴了民主的承诺。批评者非常正确地指出学生与农民之间严重的阶级差异；然而，也许联盟最好的地方正是这些差异没有使参与者气馁。我们所有人都需要一点这些城市中产阶级年轻人的浪漫主义与承诺。通过他们，为环境作为正义而动员的乌托邦主义成为一种挑战，而不是放弃的理由。

en: At one Ford-supported conference, Walter Coward, director of the Rural Poverty Alleviation Program, offered his reflections on the genesis of CBNRM during his tenure at Ford. His story stresses two conjunctures through which the idea became charismatic enough to travel. The first was his discovery of small-scale, “community-based” irrigation at precisely that moment when development agencies were obsessed with large-scale irrigation. Coward relates how Philippine villagers showed him sophisticated local systems of irrigation. International developers had ignored these small-scale systems; they wanted big dams. Small-scale irrigation could be the perfect symbol for the alternative: not Big Dams, but small dams; not Big Development, but community-based development. The political will to support local forms of resource management owes a great deal to the fact that small-scale irrigation was such an apt carrier for the idea of community (Coward forthcoming).

children: The second conjuncture was the extension of community-based irrigation to build the idea of community-based forestry. Coward told conference attendees how he arrived in Indonesia, as a Ford Foundation program officer, with ideas he had developed in the Philippines about small-scale irrigation. There he met foresters worried about forest destruction and the loss of rural livelihoods. Thinking together, they hatched a larger domain of “community-based natural resource management”: Community irrigation models could help reorganize forestry. Two kinds of charisma were gained in this articulation. First, CBNRM took off toward many resources, becoming a general resource-management model: Soon, for example, Ford was thinking about community-based fisheries. Second, a new set of allies was acquired. Conservationists were worried about forests; indigenous rights groups worried about forest communities. The Ford Foundation was not ready to endorse either conservation or indigenous rights; however, their programs gained momentum from the impetus of these overlapping causes.

zh: 在一次福特基金会支持的会议上，农村减贫项目主任 Walter Coward 谈了他对 CBNRM 在其福特任职期间起源的反思。他的叙述强调两个契机，这一观念正是通过它们获得了足以传播的感召力。第一个契机是他在发展机构正痴迷于大规模灌溉之时，发现了小规模、“以社群为基础”的灌溉。Coward 讲述了菲律宾村民如何向他展示当地复杂的灌溉系统。国际开发者曾忽视这些小规模系统；他们想要大型水坝。小规模灌溉可以成为替代方案的完美象征：不是大坝，而是小坝；不是大发展，而是以社群为基础的发展。支持地方资源管理形式的政治意愿，很大程度上归功于小规模灌溉是如此适合承载社群观念（Coward forthcoming）。

children: 第二个契机是，以社群为基础的灌溉被扩展，用以建构以社群为基础的林业观念。Coward 向与会者讲述了他作为福特基金会项目官员抵达印尼的经历，带着他在菲律宾形成的关于小规模灌溉的想法。在那里，他遇到了担忧森林破坏和乡村生计丧失的林务员。他们一起思考，构想出一个更大的“以社群为基础的自然资源管理”领域：社群灌溉模式可以帮助重组林业。这种接合获得了两种感召力。第一，CBNRM 向多种资源扩展，成为一种普遍的资源管理模式：例如，福特很快开始考虑以社群为基础的渔业。第二，获得了一批新的盟友。保护主义者担忧森林；原住民权利团体担忧森林社群。福特基金会尚未准备好为保护或原住民权利中的任何一方背书；然而，他们的项目从这些相互重叠事业的推动力中获得了势头。

en: Consider, for example, the influential Zimbabwean initiative called CAMPFIRE. CAMPFIRE offers rural communities a share of the income gained from international big game hunting if they conserve local wildlife. CAMPFIRE is a very different model of community-based conservation than that discussed so far. Rather than working to conserve resources for village use, this program offers villagers a quid pro quo: Put up with the wildlife, which compete with village cattle and destroy village crops, in exchange for a share in the sometimes considerable revenues of big game hunting. This striking arrangement brings us directly to the particularity of collaborative partners, which range from rich white hunters, willing to pay top dollars for trophies, to a national government unwilling to provide for rural citizens directly.

children: In a history of the program, CAMPFIRE’s founder, Marshall Murphree, portrays it as a set of strategic compromises in which the “congruent objectives” of allies could be tweaked into a practical arrangement (Murphree forthcoming). The compromises, he admitted, helped explain the failures of the program as well as its successes; for example, by allowing local government to count as “community,” the program became entwined with government's own corruption and inequality. Critics of CAMPFIRE have charged that the program is just too deeply intertwined with bad collaborators. Conservation for the benefit of big game hunters fits too neatly into the colonial legacy of native displacement in East Africa; government management objectives join too poorly with local empowerment (Neumann forthcoming; Matowanyika 1997). Questions about community resource management only open wider: When do contingent collaborations negate utopian hopes leaving only practical—and unworthy—solutions? When does CBNRM become a top-down management scheme?

One response to these questions assessed the influence of CAMPFIRE with a cautious optimism. Ken Wilson, a Ford Foundation program officer in Mozambique, found that the inspiration of CAMPFIRE encouraged national elites in Mozambique to support community resource management in the 1990s (Wilson forthcoming). At that time, the political climate in Mozambique differed sharply from that in Zimbabwe, in his assessment. Where Zimbabwe offered top-down management, Mozambique allowed models to “bubble up” from local sources. Community resource experiments could be worked out in relation to a more circumscribed and relevant set of players, from shamans to foresters. Communities could be negotiated closer to the ground. In Wilson’s story, CAMPFIRE facilitated a combination of local initiative and international backing.

zh: 例如，考虑一下津巴布韦颇具影响力的 CAMPFIRE 计划。如果乡村社群保护当地野生动物，CAMPFIRE 就把国际大型猎物狩猎所得收入的一部分分给它们。CAMPFIRE 是一种与本篇迄今所讨论的模式非常不同的以社群为基础的保护模式。该计划不是努力保护资源供村庄使用，而是向村民提出一种交换条件：忍受与村庄牲畜竞争并毁坏村庄作物的野生动物，以换取有时相当可观的大型猎物狩猎收入的一部分。这种引人注目的安排把我们直接带到协作伙伴的特殊性：从愿意为战利品一掷千金的富有白人猎人，到不愿直接供养乡村公民的国家政府。

children: 在该计划的一部历史中，CAMPFIRE 的创始人 Marshall Murphree 将其描绘为一系列战略妥协，在其中盟友的“一致目标”可以被调整成一种实际安排（Murphree forthcoming）。他承认，这些妥协既有助于解释该计划的失败，也有助于解释其成功；例如，由于允许地方政府算作“社群”，该计划与政府自身的腐败和不平等纠缠在一起。CAMPFIRE 的批评者指控，该计划与糟糕的合作者纠缠得过深。为大型猎物狩猎者利益服务的保护，过于契合东非原住民被驱逐的殖民遗产；政府管理目标与地方赋权的结合又过于糟糕（Neumann forthcoming; Matowanyika 1997）。关于社群资源管理的问题只会越发拓展：偶然的协作何时会否定乌托邦希望，只留下实用——却无价值——的解决方案？CBNRM 何时会变成自上而下的管理制度？

对这些问题的回应之一，以谨慎的乐观评估了 CAMPFIRE 的影响。福特基金会在莫桑比克的项目官员 Ken Wilson 发现，CAMPFIRE 的启发鼓励了莫桑比克的国家精英在1990年代支持社群资源管理（Wilson forthcoming）。据他评估，当时莫桑比克的政治气候与津巴布韦截然不同。津巴布韦提供的是自上而下的管理，而莫桑比克允许模式从地方源头“冒上来”。社群资源实验可以围绕一组更有限、也更相关的参与者来设计，从萨满到林务员。社群可以在更贴近地面的层面上被协商。在 Wilson 的叙述中，CAMPFIRE 促成了地方首创精神与国际支持的结合。

en: Agrawal (1997) offers a critical reflection on the history of concepts of “community” as these inform CBNRM. This too is a Ford Foundation supported discussion paper.
zh: Agrawal（1997）对“社群”概念的历史作了批判性反思，因为这些概念为 CBNRM 提供了基础。这也是一份福特基金会支持的讨论稿。

en: Leach and Fairhead discuss this problem in relation to West African forest histories (2000). See also Tsing (1999).
zh: Leach 和 Fairhead 结合西非森林史讨论了这一问题（2000）。另见 Tsing（1999）。
